meaning.evidence: Every fact, figure, timestamp, link and component survives unchanged (the table, "0.02154816 USDC / FOLD", "`1787148023`", the CCA rules, the safety list, all four notices). Small shifts are colour or near-synonyms: "locked in for long-term on-chain liquidity support", "stop sniping" for 'mitigate', and "or what it'll trade at" added to the risk notice.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "done and dusted", "up for grabs in the final period", "kicked in", "dodgy, unofficial sources", "land in your DMs out of the blue". "stop sniping" overstates 'mitigate', and "locked in" slightly overstates 'committed'.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Aussie plain English: "It's for folks who had a go in", "No one can tell you what the market price will do down the track", "Have a read of the full".

register.evidence: A light level-3 touch, perhaps a shade light: idiom is sprinkled ("Nope.", "Yep.", "done and dusted") but much reads as plain English ("The auction runs over a number of separate periods."). No swearing, fitting vulgarity 1 on a financial FAQ.

tone.evidence: Keeps the careful, official FAQ tone; the safety warnings stay firm ("will never, ever ask for your seed phrase").

flow.evidence: Reads cleanly: "The CCA hands out tokens bit by bit and uses the one price for everyone within each period."

variety.evidence: Varied ("done and dusted", "up for grabs", "gas wars", "kicked in", "dodgy"), with "kicked in"/"kicked off" and "had a go" recurring.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the FOLD Auction FAQ, structure, callouts and notices intact.
